headline: Sharks’ Marchment fined for roughing Islanders’ Eklund
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Sharks forward Marchment was given a pair of minor penalties for roughing Islanders player Eklund on Monday night. The headline says he was fined for the play, but the summary gives no amount and nothing about further discipline.

The bigger question for SJS is what its numbers say about the team. San Jose sits at 8-11-1 and has taken only 43% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, with a gap of minus 11.5 between the goals it has scored and the goals its chances suggest it should have. Its goalies have bailed it out, though, saving 10.3 goals more than expected. NYI looks steadier at 7-6-4, holding 46% of the expected goals, but it also leans on its goaltending, which has saved 11 goals above expected. Both teams are living on their goalies, and with the Sharks' penalty kill allowing 1.03 expected goals per game, giving opponents power plays is a habit they can least afford.
